speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this dry cough going on for about two months now. It doesn't bring up any phlegm or blood, but I do notice I get short of breath when I try to move around and there's a whistling sound when I breathe. However, there is no time for labs. The patient will deteriorate before results return. Diagnose the cardiac condition now from current presentation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with possible underlying cardiac strain. Given the dry cough, exertional dyspnea, and wheezing without productive sputum, this presentation is most consistent with obstructive lung disease rather than primary cardiac failure, though right-sided heart strain cannot be fully excluded without imaging. Immediate management should focus on bronchodilators and oxygen therapy while monitoring for respiratory failure.
